scope: Independent static visual review of repaired directional gait only; not a full v2 acceptance review.

evidence.pose_continuity: The current eight-frame row uses a compact sequence of overlapping, opening and closing leg poses. It removes the old row's conspicuous changes between long airborne strides and a near-upright endpoint.
evidence.alternation: In the static sequence the bent forearms move through different forward/back positions, and the two shoes pass through overlap and separation. The visible pose family is compatible with near/far limb alternation; exact joint phase is not measurable from this opaque contact sheet alone.
evidence.identity_and_head: Hair, glasses, face, head size and upper-body proportions stay visually stable throughout all eight repaired frames.
evidence.attachments: Shoulder, neck, elbow, knee and shoe connections remain attached. No major detached limb, empty interior gap or broken silhouette is visible at the displayed sprite scale.
evidence.clipping: All repaired poses remain fully inside their slots. The mirrored left-facing sequence retains the same compact pose family.

accepted_warnings: The shorter stride reads as gentle shuffling or a very soft jog; it is less energetic than the original long-stride art.
Some pant cuffs and shoe joins look angular in the enlarged row, but they do not form a major disconnected seam at normal pet size.
The opaque dark pants and overlapping shoes limit anatomical near/far attribution in static images. Parent joint invariants are needed to confirm exact alternation.
limitations: Only ordered static frames were inspected. No GIF or real-time animation was observed in this review.
Static contact sheets cannot certify perceived smoothness at the native 120 ms x 7 plus 220 ms timing, especially the wraparound hold; parent playback verification remains necessary.
Unmodified non-directional rows were inspected only for overall context, and look-direction rows were outside scope.
